name: statutory-staleness-fl
title: Statutory Staleness in Florida Appellate Construction Holdings
description: One row per (decision, statutory section) pair where a Florida appellate court construed the meaning of a Florida statute, with whether that section has been amended since the decision and, where two editions of the code are held, whether the operative text actually changed. A citator reports whether a case was overruled by another case; it is far weaker on the other way a holding dies, which is that the legislature amended the statute and no court has had occasion to say so. This dataset measures that gap directly.

sources.title: CourtListener bulk export, topped up nightly from the courts

fields.name: cites
fields.description: times the decision has been cited, per CourtListener

fields.name: last_amended
fields.description: most recent amendment year in the section history trail

fields.name: amendments_since
fields.description: count of amendments after the decision

fields.name: gap_years
fields.description: years between the decision and the most recent later amendment

fields.name: exposed
fields.description: 1 where the section was amended after the decision; an UPPER BOUND, not a finding of abrogation

fields.name: tier
fields.description: amendment-screen | text-diff -- text-diff is only available where an edition at or before the decision year is held

fields.name: text_changed
fields.description: 1 where the operative text differs between the edition in force at the decision and the current edition; null outside the text-diff tier

fields.name: similarity
fields.description: SequenceMatcher ratio between the two editions operative text, history trail excluded

fields.name: edition_at_decision
fields.description: the statute edition used as the baseline for the diff

fields.name: sentence
fields.description: the sentence in which the section was construed, verbatim

fields.name: statement
fields.description: the row written as one self-contained English sentence

run.query: (ambiguous OR ambiguity OR ambiguities OR construe OR construed OR construction OR interpret OR interpreted OR interpretation OR "plain meaning" OR "legislative intent" OR "rules of statutory construction")
